subject: Calculate theta one item at a time, without the GUI

messages.author: eb16076e3c2de08c
messages.subject: Calculate theta one item at a time, without the GUI
parts:
Dear Phil,

For given item parameters, is it possible to manually provide item responses one at a time and calculate interim theta estimations as each item is responded to? This is possible when using the GUI but I can only seem to get theta estimations once the test is completed. Is it possible to calculate thetas_history and thetas_SE_history from items administered one by one, without the GUI? 

Best wishes,

Conrad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Calculate theta one item at a time, without the GUI
parts:
Hi Conrad,

Sorry for the delay; life is pretty wild right now now at home/work (a line that's pretty blurry these days....). There's various ways that I can answer this question, so I might need more background information. Are you trying to make a CAT implementation yourself, or are you just trying to track how theta changes over time in a more interest-sake way? If the latter, you can just use mirt::fscores() and supply an observed pattern to the response.pattern input, which mostly will consist of NA placeholders for items that have no response. If the former, functions like updateDesign() showcase how one can explore some of the internally manipulated functions used in calls to mirtCAT() in a more interactive way, though what you are looking for may require a bit more exposure of the specific internals (I've chosen not to export everything for front-end users to play with since things could get complicated very quickly). HTH, though let me know if you require further clarification. 

Phil

parts:
Dear Phil, 

Just following up on this because I am quite keen on using mirtCAT() in Concerto for some of my tests. 
I created a simple logic to try out the functions but it seems to throw an error at the 11th item that I don't quite understand. I don't have any negative length vectors. 
The reproducible code is below. 

Error in updateDesign(CATdesign, items = item_administered, responses = resp,  : 
  negative length vectors are not allowed
In addition: Warning message:
In min(which(is.na(x$person$items_answered))) :
  no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf


Also just some additional questions. 
  1. When providing the item parameters (difficulty) for the generate.mirt_object(), do we provide the slope-intercept form or the classic IRT parameterization form? How would the generate.mirt_object() know which form we provide? 
  2. Can we activate the mirtCAT() without providing the plaus_resp object for the first item? 
  3. I am aware that we can manually select the start item or based it on the item criteria approach. But how do I select the first item based on item difficulty values? i.e. I would like the first item (for any item bank) to be one that is around 1SD above 0.  

# create mo from estimated parameters
set.seed(1234)
nitems <- 50
itemnames <- paste0('Item.', 1:nitems)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3))
d <- matrix(rnorm(nitems))
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = 'dich')
mod <- mirt(dat, 1)
icoef =coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)

# run locally, random response pattern given Theta
(plaus_resp <- generate_pattern(mod, 0))
CATdesign <- mirtCAT(mo = mod,local_pattern=plaus_resp, criteria = 'MI', design_elements = TRUE,
                     method = 'MAP', start_item = "MI") #adaptive, MI starting item

# create for loop logic
(response=sample(0,1, nitems, replace = TRUE))
item_vector=rep(NA,nrow(icoef$items))
resp_pattern = NULL
item_administered = NULL
theta_history= NULL
thetaSE_history = NULL

for(i in 1:nitems){
  
   # find next item
  (new_item <- findNextItem(CATdesign))
  
  # save administered items
  (item_administered=c(item_administered, new_item))
  
  # record responses to items
  item_vector[[new_item]] = response[i] # single response
  
  # save responses sequentially
  (resp_pattern = c(resp_pattern,response[i])) # save response
  
  # update theta
  updated_theta = fscores(mod, method = "EAP", response.pattern = item_vector)
  (theta=updated_theta[,'F1'])
  (thetaSE=updated_theta[,'SE_F1'])
  
  # theta history
  theta_history = c(theta_history, theta)
  thetaSE_history = c(thetaSE_history, thetaSE)
  
  # update cat design
  CATdesign <- updateDesign(CATdesign, items = item_administered, responses = resp_pattern, Theta = theta)
  
}


Kind regards,
Aiden

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Calculate theta one item at a time, without the GUI
parts:
Hi Aiden,

Your code seems to break here:
(resp_pattern = c(resp_pattern,response[i])) # save response

where response[i] doesn't work since it seems to only have one element. I think you meant to use

(response=sample(0:1, nitems, replace = TRUE))

instead of
(response=sample(0,1, nitems, replace = TRUE))
Regarding your questions
1. Can we activate the mirtCAT() without providing the plaus_resp object for the first item?
Wouldn't plaus_resp just be a vector placeholder on the first iteration? I'm not sure why including it would be initially difficult.

1. I am aware that we can manually select the start item or based it on the item criteria approach. But how do I select the first item based on item difficulty values? i.e. I would like the first item (for any item bank) to be one that is around 1SD above 0.

Just do this computation manually and locate the item difficulty yourself. I.e., extract the difficulty parameters (coef(mod, IRTpars = TRUE, simplify=TRUE)), locate the value that meets your criteria, and select this as the manual starting item. That's part of the reason why mirtCAT() allows for manual specification of the first item rather than forcing a particular first item criteria (such as selecting the maximum information item). HTH.

Phil

Kind regards,
Aiden

messages.subject: Re: Calculate theta one item at a time, without the GUI
parts:
Thanks, I was able to reproduce the problem. Rather than trying to fix it though I decided that the argument structure for updateDesign() was pretty awkward, so it's now been reworked on the dev version to force only one item updating at a time rather than requiring users to track the vector responses. This seems quite a bit more natural, and allows more safety in the implementation. Please install the dev version and check out the new form, and let me know if you would like additional components exposed as well. 

As well, you no longer have to supply a dummy local pattern input on the initial definition through mirtCAT() (I too found that annoying while testing). HTH.

Phil
